question.prompt:
A number of linked rings, each \(1\) cm thick, are hanging on a peg. The top ring has an outside diameter of \(20\) cm. The outside diameter of each of the other rings is \(1\) cm less than that of the ring above it. The bottom ring has an outside diameter of \(3\) cm. What is the distance, in cm, from the top of the top ring to the bottom of the bottom ring?

[Figure 1](figures/2006_AMC_12A_Q12_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
[Figure 1](figures/2006_AMC_12A_Q12_question_fig1.svg)

The thickness matters at every link. The inner top of a lower ring rests against the inner bottom of the ring above it. Each contact edge is \(1\) cm from its corresponding outside extreme, so the lower ring's outside top is \(2\) cm above the upper ring's outside bottom. Consequently, each ring after the first adds its outside diameter minus \(2\) cm to the chain's length.

The outside diameters are \(20,19,\ldots,3\), so there are
\[
20-3+1=18
\]
rings and \(17\) links. To add the diameters, pair the largest with the smallest: \(20+3=23\), \(19+4=23\), and so on. All \(18\) diameters occur once in these \(9\) pairs, giving a sum of \(9\cdot23=207\) cm.

Subtracting \(2\) cm for each link gives the required distance:
\[
207-2\cdot17=\boxed{173\text{ cm}}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Add diameters and account for each link
